prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the best one for you depends on your goals, budget, industry, channel mix and whether you need creative, performance, product/UX, or full-service marketing.

If you tell me what you need I can recommend a short, tailored list. Meanwhile, here are (a) common client needs and the kinds of agencies that tend to excel, (b) several well-regarded agencies with San Francisco presence, and (c) quick tips for choosing.

1) Match by need
- Performance marketing / paid media / growth: look for agencies strong in PPC, paid social, CRO and attribution.  
- Creative & brand campaigns: look for award-winning creative shops with strong production and storytelling.  
- Product/UX & digital experience: look for digital product studios that combine UX, design and engineering.  
- Full-service / integrated: agencies that run strategy → creative → media → analytics end-to-end.

2) Agencies with a strong San Francisco presence (examples)
- Goodby Silverstein & Partners — creative-led campaigns and brand advertising (SF-based).  
- AKQA — digital product, experience design and campaigns.  
- R/GA — digital transformation, creative and technology-driven marketing.  
- Razorfish — digital marketing, media and experience services.  
- Jellyfish — paid media, analytics and programmatic, global digital services with SF office.  
- Wpromote — performance marketing and growth-focused services (has SF office).

(These are examples of reputable options with SF operations; there are many excellent boutique and specialist firms too.)

3) How to choose quickly
- Ask for case studies with measurable results for clients in your industry.  
- Check client retention and references.  
- Verify tools/tech stack and reporting cadence.  
- Confirm team members who will do the work (not just senior salespeople).  
- Get a pilot or short trial engagement before committing long term.  
- Use directories/reviews: Clutch.co, Agency Spotter, G2, LinkedIn, Google Partner listings.

If you want, tell me: your primary goals (brand, growth, top-funnel vs. performance), monthly marketing budget, industry, and timeline — I’ll shortlist 3–5 San Francisco agencies that fit and can draft an outreach/RFP you can send.
